verdicts.evidence: PAPER.md:146–162 replaces the false converse with a support-only hull theorem, feasible-distribution linear programs, dual certificates and a facial-support characterization. Line 160 includes the six-profile counterexample. The independent full rerun reproduces the exhaustive comparisons and certificate checks.

PAPER.md:9,19,55,78–80 explicitly require the unrestricted product domain. The claim that empirical correlation/distance maps reveal compatible combinations is removed. Lines 204–206 distinguish commitment compatibility from what survey correlations and respondent distances preserve.

PAPER.md:174 and simulation/atlas/empirical.py:190–215 apply researcher eligibility and repeat-participation screening. The independent rerun reproduces 232 eligible submissions, 166 conference respondents and 223 complete respondents in each analysed battery. Downstream analyses use the corrected samples.

PAPER.md:176,188,190 and empirical.py:32–49 replace independent-fold standard errors with the corrected resampled variance, (1/J + n_test/n_train)s², and Student-t intervals. The rerun reproduces the position-battery pairwise SE 0.06097547 and third-order interval [−0.07780960, 0.00065734].

PAPER.md:188,194–196 separates prespecified-triplet power from screening power. empirical.py:384–470 repeats tuning, null fitting, Monte Carlo testing and BH screening on planted datasets. With 9,999 draws, the minimum p-value is 0.0001, below 0.05/165. Recomputed screening detects the trolley-sized target in 0/100 datasets. The FDR-guarantee wording is a separate remaining issue.

PAPER.md:192,194,210 replaces exclusion with non-detection and limited sensitivity. Recomputed simultaneous intervals all contain zero, and none excludes the trolley interaction magnitude. Their minimum half-width is 2.08074. The conclusion acknowledges that trolley-sized effects would probably be missed.

PAPER.md:45–49 now requires a closure system containing Ω and closed under arbitrary intersections, defines closure by intersection, states the obstruction-free convention and explains the open-interval counterexample. The missing hypothesis is repaired.
PAPER.md:9 and 19 now assign order n+1 to categorical answers together with implications. Table 1 and line 86 retain order one for implications alone.

new_problems.problem: The new source claim and revised figure caption assert achieved 5% false-discovery control without establishing the assumptions needed for that guarantee.
new_problems.evidence: The [Benjamini–Hochberg abstract](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x) proves control for independent statistics. These overlapping triplets share observations, items and a fitted null; no applicable dependence argument is supplied. A false discovery in four of 100 datasets under one fitted global null does not establish general 5% control. Describe nominal BH screening or justify the guarantee.

new_problems.problem: The probability lower bound is rounded upward: “at least 0.027” is not established for every unobserved profile.
new_problems.evidence: simulation/output/results.json at /consciousness/positions/lp_bounds/smallest_positive_bound is 0.026905829596400074, reproduced independently. This is approximately 0.027 but strictly below it. Use an approximation or round the lower bound downward.

new_problems.problem: The new power paragraph says there were 100 simulated datasets per effect size, although the two largest levels used 75.
new_problems.evidence: Recomputed /consciousness/positions/discovery_power/levels/*/datasets is [100,100,100,100,75,75]. Figure 2’s caption states the exception correctly; the prose and its bound passage should state it too.

new_problems.problem: The rewritten conclusion treats an 80% power threshold as a hard detection threshold by saying the scan would find “only” effects about three times as strong.
new_problems.evidence: Line 200 reports 80% power at 0.0144 bits, approximately three times 0.0048866657. Smaller effects retain nonzero detection probability. State the effect size required for approximately 80% power instead.

claims_coverage.note: All 285 existing bound passages occur in the revised manuscript, and all 162 computation claims match the recorded results after declared rounding/scaling. Coverage nevertheless misses these occurrences, especially number words, repeated quantities and the new Figure 2 caption. Labels, citation years, dates, identifiers, name-like compounds and constants inside mathematical expressions were excluded.

Inspected equation (3.1), stating invariance under taking intersections. [Averkov](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6179v3).

Inspected the products and axis-parallel-box discussion on p. 144. It supports the pairwise-intersection property used here. [Danzer et al.](https://www3.nd.edu/~andyp/teaching/2013SpringMath366/DanzerGruenbaumKlee.pdf).
Inspected Theorem 2.2: pairwise intersection suffices for axis-parallel boxes. [Amenta et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.07606v2).

Inspected Proposition 3.1 and the lattice discussion: convex restriction cannot increase the Helly number, and the unit-cell construction attains the grid bound. [Averkov](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6179v3).
Inspected Lemma 2.6, relating the discrete Helly number to empty convex polytopes. [Amenta et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.07606v2).

The [OpenAlex record](https://api.openalex.org/works/W134663479) identifies the article and DOI 10.5169/seals-32945. The original supporting pages were inaccessible. Later inspected papers corroborate the result but do not verify this source directly.

Inspected Theorem 1 and its general-position hypothesis. It establishes the 30-point empty-hexagon threshold; I did not rerun the external computer-assisted proof. [Heule et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.00737v1).

Inspected the opening result and construction: arbitrarily large general-position sets without empty convex heptagons exist. contribution_after.assessment: The paper organizes established Helly, constraint-satisfaction and marginal-polytope results into a useful account of philosophical maps; the repaired facial-support characterization is established geometry. Its additional contribution is the reproducible comparison of support versus numerical exclusions and new descriptive survey analyses, whose scope is now substantially better calibrated.

summary: All eight referee findings are closed. The independent rerun passes 34 tests and reproduces every substantive result. All five added references match Crossref; the abstract has 246 words; no prohibited self-reference or material visual defect was found. Remaining issues concern the FDR guarantee, numerical/power wording and incomplete claim bindings. Source review yields 61 supported, three unsupported and seven not-checkable claims. The availability section identifies the correct OSF datasets and unstated licences, but the unchanged [GitHub repository](https://github.com/piatra-institute/papers-beyond-philosophical-distance) returns unauthenticated HTTP 404, leaving public code availability unverified.
